W2 (empirical), after E029. Tip is E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 (20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%, 8.75 true epochs, 219 steps at batch 2000). It clears 0.753 on seeds 0-2 by about 0.17 pp. E029 reports a held-out mean of 0.7526, which is below the bar, so the tip's real margin is about zero or negative.

Measured chain (time/accuracy): E004 compiled 9.04/0.7486. E005 +EMA 9.10/0.7583. E006 +Muon 9.45/0.7649. E007 progressive resizing 7.33/0.7590. E010 last group 512 6.64/0.7548. E015 CUDA graphs 6.58/0.7574. E017 break-free 6.55/0.7537. E018 24/32 only 5.99/0.7502. E020 -1 epoch 5.86/0.7528. E021 group 2 at 320 6.04/0.7530. E023 -0.5 epoch 6.20/0.7538. E024 26 px middle phase 6.07/0.7510. E025 EMA exponent 2 6.20/0.7557. E026 20 px first phase 6.02/0.7540. E027 8.75 epochs 5.88/0.7547. E028 FreezeOut 5.36/0.7517. E029 faster warm-up 5.86/0.7526 (discard).

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, at a cost of 0.0-0.15 pp. It is the cheapest lever, but the tip is now at the accuracy floor. E020, E023, E027.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp) and Muon (+0.66 pp) are already in the tip. E005, E006.
3. Time tracks pixels and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. An early low-res phase is nearly free (E026). Removing or shrinking the 28 px phase costs 0.3-0.5 pp (E018, E024).
4. Compute cuts on the 32 px tail cost about 0.3 pp per 0.5 s (E028).
5. wd, label smoothing, Muon lr, LR floor, EMA exponent and warm-up are flat within noise (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025, E029). E016's 0.7607 was a lucky draw.
6. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to RNG use or step count reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. The held-out 10-seed mean sits about 0.2 pp below the seeds 0-2 mean for recent tips. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I have overpredicted time on trims. Savings are 2-5% larger than modelled. Accuracy deltas under 0.3 pp are unreadable, and I have been consistently slightly optimistic on accuracy for the structural changes.

Unsure: whether any time-neutral booster exists. Whether the tip must regain accuracy (more epochs) to be safely feasible. Whether per-sample loss tracking adds overhead.

forecasts.reason: Dropping 10% easy samples is like a uniform epoch cut, with extra scatter/topk overhead; the base is E023 (6.20), so about 8.9% fewer steps gives about 5.75 s, at accuracy near E020/E023.
The interval change is time-neutral; the knobs measured so far are flat, so the effect is below noise.
The loss-only change has no time effect; the accuracy effect is small and sign-uncertain.
Moving 15% of steps from 24 px to 20 px saves about 3% of time; the accuracy cost is likely small but the bar is already tight.
Per-resolution whitening adds a little prepare cost and has an unmeasured, probably small effect.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 40-seed mean? If it is below 0.75 (held-out 0.7526 suggests a margin of about 0.2 pp), the time cuts must stop or be funded by a real accuracy gain.
Is any time-neutral accuracy booster real (above 0.15 pp held-out)? Every knob tried so far has been flat.
Does the early low-res phase stay free when extended (20 px share beyond 15%)? That is the remaining cheap time lever.
